Question 1

A=[2−134−17−24−3]

If A=LU is the LU decomposition of the matrix A given above, what is the value of l21⋅u33?

a
−6
b
−14
c
12
d
0
e
10
Submit

decision.explanation: Eliminating the first entry of row 2 gives l21=4/2=2 and row 2 becomes [0,1,1]. Adding row 1 to row 3 gives [0,3,0]; subtracting 3 times the new row 2 gives [0,0,-3]. Thus u33=-3 and l21·u33=2(-3)=-6.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 & 7 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{33}?$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 & 7 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ \,\,2\,\, & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+1{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ \,\,2\,\, & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ \,\,2\,\, & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & \,3\, & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{21}=2$ and ${u}_{33}=-3,$ we get

$$
{l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{33}=2\cdot (-3)=-6.
$$

decision.explanation: The first elimination multiplier is l21=4/(-1)=-4. Applying R2 := R2+4R1 gives [0,-6,-7], so u22=-6. Row 3 has second entry 3, hence l32=3/(-6)=-1/2. Therefore l32·u22=(-1/2)(-6)=3.

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

If $C=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $C$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{22}?$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $C$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ -4 & -6 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ -4 & -6 & -7 \\ \,\,0\,\, & -\frac{1}{2} & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{32}=-\frac{1}{2}$ and ${u}_{22}=-6,$ we get

$$
{l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{22}=(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (-6)=3.
$$
